lesson_topic: Intellectual Property Law — The Bundle of Rights Model (Introductory Module)

principles.evidence: No non-decorative graphics, diagrams, charts, or illustrations are present across any of the five slides; all slides consist entirely of on-screen prose text. The visual channel carries zero informational graphics, making reciprocity between visual and verbal channels structurally impossible.

On-screen text across all slides consists of full paragraph-length sentences running three to four lines each, far exceeding keyword or short-phrase density. The transcript is verbatim identical to the on-screen text on every slide, with zero elaboration, paraphrase, or differentiation between channels.

All complex descriptions are delivered exclusively through dense on-screen prose rather than narration supplementing a visual; the visual channel functions solely as a text display medium. The narration is a verbatim read-aloud of the on-screen paragraphs on every slide, constituting a direct violation of the modality principle across the entire deck.

No decorative clipart, stock filler, or extraneous tangential content is present; the text content remains topically focused on the bundle-of-rights framework throughout. Slide backgrounds appear clean and uncluttered, and typography is consistent, though the absence of any graphics limits the observable range of coherence violations.

No visual cues such as arrows, highlights, color contrast, bold text, or callouts are present to mark key elements on any slide; the only structural differentiation is a title heading on each slide. The narration does not employ verbal signaling phrases to direct learner attention, and no single key takeaway is explicitly emphasized or isolated on any slide.

No graphics, labels, captions, or figures are present on any slide, rendering the majority of spatial contiguity criteria unobservable and thus unmet by default. Text and visual referents are never paired because no visual referents exist; the layout is text-block only with title and body separated by conventional slide structure.
